  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32775v1</id>
    <title>Large profinite genus and extensions in Bestvina-Brady groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T15:24:44Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32775v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32775v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We construct the first examples of uncountable families of residually finite duality groups of type $FP$, all of which have isomorphic profinite completions, while being pairwise not quasi-isometric. To establish these finiteness properties, we prove conjectures of Leary regarding groups of deck transformations of certain cubical branched covers being residually finite and virtually special. The main new tool is a strong separability result for Bestvina-Brady groups, allowing the extension of any finite quotient of many Bestvina-Brady subgroups to a finite quotient of the whole group. This gives a finite version of the congruence extension property, which we also establish for the same group pairs.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32761v1</id>
    <title>The restricted Hurwitz action on cameral decompositions of Coxeter elements</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T15:04:27Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32761v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32761v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Given a dual Coxeter system (W, T) of rank n, the Hurwitz action of the braid group on the reduced T-decompositions of a Coxeter element is transitive. When we choose a geometric representation of W, the reflections with respect to the n walls of one given chamber form a generating set S that we call cameral. An ordering of S is called a cameral decomposition and the product a cameral Coxeter element, which depends only on the quiver obtained by orienting the Coxeter diagram with vertices S according to the ordering. We show that the reduced decompositions of a cameral Coxeter elements for which the underlying set S satisfies that (W, S ) is a Coxeter system, are necessarily cameral, and we count the number of chambers from which a cameral Coxeter element can be obtained. We show that one can go through all these chambers using the restricted Hurwitz action on the set of cameral decompositions, which is generated by transpositions of adjacent commuting reflections and by the Garside element δ of the dual Garside structure, which acts by a quiver mutation of the orientation of the Coxeter diagram.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32680v1</id>
    <title>Realizable Cohomology Classes of Dihedral and Generalized Quaternion Groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T14:15:50Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32680v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32680v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We compute the Chern classes of irreducible representations for the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ and the generalized quaternion groups $Q_{2^n}$. Utilizing these computations, we investigate whether every even-dimensional class in the integral group cohomology of these families can be realized as a Chern class of some complex representation. It turns out that this realizability question answers in the affirmative for the generalized quaternion groups. In contrast, it turns out that the answer for dihedral groups is erratic.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32643v1</id>
    <title>Split Frobenius Groups, Equational Domains, $\mathfrak{X}T$- and $CS\mathfrak{X}$-groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T13:52:59Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32643v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32643v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We investigate conditions under which a semidirect product $G=HN$, and in particular a restricted wreath product, is an equational domain. For a variety of groups $\X$, we study semidirect products of $\XT$-groups (groups where $\langle A, B\rangle \in\X$ for any two $\X$-subgroups $A$ and $B$ with nontrivial intersection) and $\CSX$-groups (groups where all maximal $\X$-subgroups are malnormal). We pay particular attention to split Frobenius groups and investigate conditions under which such groups are $\XT$- or $\CSX$-groups.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32426v1</id>
    <title>Associative Lifts of CW Semigroups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T09:51:57Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32426v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32426v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Every nonempty connected finite-dimensional CW topological semigroup admits a continuous associative multiplication on its universal cover that lifts the multiplication of the base. Such a multiplication is unique up to a deck transformation: in fact, any two associative lifts are conjugate whenever they exist. We show that the finite-dimensional hypothesis cannot be dropped in general: a connected, countable, infinite-dimensional CW topological semigroup is constructed for which continuous lifts of multiplication exist, but none is associative. The counterexample has nonabelian fundamental group isomorphic to Thompson's group $F$. Thus finite dimensionality is sufficient for associative lifting in the CW setting, whereas the unrestricted infinite-dimensional statement fails.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32395v1</id>
    <title>A New Characterisation of Selflessness</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T09:20:38Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32395v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32395v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We characterise the existence of expectation-preserving embeddings of reduced amalgamated free product $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras into norm ultrapowers of the first factor, fixing its diagonal copy pointwise, in terms of complementary compression relations on Hilbert space ultrapowers. This yields new characterisations of Robert's notion of selflessness, selfless inclusions, and relative selflessness with respect to conditional expectations. We also characterise Ozawa's notion of complete selflessness, including its extension to inclusions. We then illustrate the usefulness of these characterisations by establishing complete selflessness for suitable reduced (amalgamated) free products, free Araki--Woods $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras, certain Hecke $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras, and $q$-Gaussian $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras. Finally, we obtain dynamical characterisations of (complete) $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-selflessness of discrete groups and establish relative selflessness for suitable reduced crossed products.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32352v1</id>
    <title>Cofinite integral braces and crystallographic groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T08:46:15Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32352v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32352v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>A left brace is cofinite integral (CIB) if its additive group is free abelian of finite rank and its quotient by the socle is finite. Rump introduced such braces and showed that the multiplicative group of every CIB is a crystallographic group. We study CIBs from the point of view of crystallographic groups. We prove an analogue of the Bieberbach theorems: in each dimension there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of CIBs. For a fixed crystallographic group, we show that its CIB structures correspond to the orbits of a finite group action on a set of bijective 1-cocycles. We use this description to develop algorithms that enumerate them. Finally, we give a complete census of CIBs on crystallographic and Bieberbach groups up to dimension 6.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32351v1</id>
    <title>Cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T08:45:46Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32351v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32351v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>A graph is edge-transitive if its automorphism group acts transitively on its edge set. This paper is devoted to a systematic study of cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$, where $p$ is a prime and $\ell$ is an even integer. We first show that either $Γ$ is the unique cubic edge-transitive graph of order $18$, or its full automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(Γ)$ contains a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ which is isomorphic to either $Z_{p^2}$ or $Z_{p}^2$. For the case $P\cong Z_{p^2}$, we prove that $Γ$ is either arc-regular or edge-regular, and provide a complete classification of such graphs. For the case $P\cong Z_{p}^2$, we prove that $Γ$ is a normal cover of certain known graphs. This work generalizes previous classifications by Zhou and Feng (2024), Lu et al.~(2004), and others. As an application, we obtain a classification of cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$ in the case where $\ell$ is square-free.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32064v1</id>
    <title>Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T01:59:33Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32064v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32064v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $μ=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere. Consequently, \[ H_0(\Sing R;\Z)\cong H_2(\Sing R;\Z)\cong\Z^μ, \] and all remaining homology groups vanish. Thus both nonzero Betti numbers equal the first Betti number of the Milnor fiber of the plane curve singularity $z^p+w^q=0$, namely its Milnor number $μ$.</summary>
    <category term="math.GT" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31961v1</id>
    <title>Spectrum of the basilica group and the associated real and complex 2D dynamics</title>
    <updated>2026-10-22T22:10:22Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31961v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.31961v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>In this paper, we study the iteration over the real and complex loci of a specific rational map, found by Grigorchuk and Zuk. This two dimensional map arises as the renormalization map which yields the density of states measure associated with the iterated monodromy group of the Basilica Julia set. It admits two natural complex currents, and we construct their real analogs and show that they are laminar. Finally, this yields some consequences on the properties of the density of states measures and its support.</summary>
